graph_block_shuffle — CONNGRAPH dimension op

• Data kinds: conn_graph × labels → conn_graph

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.graph_block_shuffle(W: 'Any', labels: 'Any', seed: 'int' = 0) -> 'np.ndarray' (to call the implementation directly, import conngraph; conngraph.graph_block_shuffle(W: 'Any', labels: 'Any', seed: 'int' = 0) -> 'np.ndarray'; from the registry, opsconngraph.get("graph_block_shuffle"))

Usage

A control conn_graph in which the senders are shuffled within each block of layers (labels): it keeps the multiset of weights each receiver gets and the total amount of wiring between layers, and destroys only the "from whom".

Whereas graph_degree_preserving_shuffle preserves the overall degree sequence, this one preserves the layer structure (the blocks brain → neck → ventral nerve cord → muscle are not moved; rows are permuted within each block). Used as a control that keeps the effects of layer size and convergence (fan-in) and removes only "the specificity of the wiring". Reproducible with the same seed.
